Global Blocks

Change it once. It changes everywhere — and every reader finds out.

The problem

Nothing stays canonical.

You fix it — but one stale file never hears.
An agent finds it later, and the old answer spreads downstream all over again.

In the wild: one poisoned document planted dozens of fake memories in ChatGPT —
and they persisted into every future session · Johann Rehberger, disclosed May 2024

copies rot silently
Take it with you

It’s open source.

claude plugin marketplace add Playful-Sincerity/global-blocks
claude plugin install global-blocks@playful-sincerity

Apache-2.0 · two commands, in case you’d like to follow along.

every version fingerprinted · portals, not copies · whoever read it gets told
plain files · no database · no registry
The hook
the wiring — hooks.json
"PostToolUse": [
  { "matcher": "Read",
    "hooks": [ "…/transclude.py" ] } ],
"UserPromptSubmit": [
  { "hooks": [ "…/check-stale.py" ] } ]
every file read · every turn
what it injects — verbatim, from a real session
-- global-blocks · something you are
   holding moved --
 ↳ "launch-date" — you have v1;
   now at v2.  removed: March 3rd
              added: March 17th
 What you hold is unknown now, not
 false. Re-read before relying on it.

No tool call. No request. The update lands in the agent’s context on its next breath.

Precedent

None of this is new.

1960s transclusion — Ted Nelson  ·  1980s cache coherence — a stale copy is told, in silicon
2000s content addressing — git  ·  push-on-change at Wikipedia scale — MediaWiki

Every layer is decades-proven.
We point it at the claims agents share with each other.

boring is good
Why

When the info changes,
every reader finds out.

Teleport changes across your files and systems — instantly.
A plugin on one machine today — built to become a protocol for the internet.
